title: Linguistic Relativity and Why a Second Language Changes How You Think
explainer: The idea that the language you speak shapes how you perceive and reason, known as linguistic relativity (loosely, the Sapir–Whorf hypothesis), is a genuine and still-studied topic in linguistics and cognitive science; the strongest version, that language rigidly determines thought, hasn't held up, but weaker effects on perception and categorization are well supported. Computer scientist Alan Perlis made essentially the same claim about programming languages in a widely cited 1982 line, "A language that doesn't affect the way you think about programming is not worth knowing," which is the whole premise behind deliberately learning a second language for contrast.
